title: The Readout Condition: Distinguishability, Access, and Epistemic Warrant
desc: Claims routinely distinguish more finely than the access sources invoked on their behalf. The central epistemic problem is not merely whether the resulting claim is true or justified, but whether each distinction in it is correctly attributed to the source, model, background evidence, relevance restriction, or decision rule that actually supplied the discrimination. This paper develops the Readout Condition as a necessary architecture for source-relative epistemic warrant. Its core is a threepart norm: existence (every claim-level distinction has an epistemic provenance path), attribution (a distinction credited to a source must be licensed by that source), and disclosure (essential augmentations must remain visible to audit). In the exact functional case, source attribution requires constancy on readout fibers and hence factorization through the readout. For non-transitive indiscriminability, the correct extension is pointwise: a claim token at an actual alternative is licensed only if its local indiscriminability neighbourhood lies inside the claim-value fiber, avoiding an illicit transitive closure. The standard answers — the double bottom line, earned income, legitimacy, policy access, hybrid innovation — are true of most social enterprises and constitutive of none. This paper identifies a class of social enterprise for which the form is not a choice but a structural necessity, and supplies a diagnostic by which any organisation can determine whether it belongs to that class. Approach. Conceptual and comparative-institutional, grounded in a readout-relative epistemology: every record an institution holds about a person is a bounded readout of that person’s state, never the state itself, and distinctions collapsed by an early readout cannot be recovered by later readers. From this the paper defines positional governance — the capacity of an actor that holds a transaction to bind itself, credibly and enforceably, against the completion incentive of that same transaction — and the position-holding enterprise, whose product is a condition on a transaction that would otherwise proceed unconditioned. A counterfactual removal test locates the mechanism; nine requirements are derived and tested against five institutional archetypes; four mechanisms of fit are specified. title: Faqr, Scholarly Authority, and Non-Transferable Responsibility
desc: This article develops a revelation-bounded Sunni conceptual-normative architecture for relating divine normativity, juristic expertise, moral agency, and collective consultation without collapsing one into another. Its point of departure is faqr: the creaturely condition of dependence upon God. The argument reconstructs faqr as an epistemic discipline as well as a spiritual truth. Revelation is not fallible, but human reception, interpretation, contextualization, and institutionalization remain creaturely acts. The article therefore distinguishes revelation from juristic readouts, scholarly epistemic authority from adjudicative and political authority, and all of these from the agent’s answerability for action. Drawing on Qur’anic passages, the authoritative Prophetic Sunnah as accessed through Sunni hadith transmission and authentication, classical uṣūl al-fiqh, distinctions among fatwā, qạ̄a’, ijtihād, and taqlīd, and modern scholarship on Islamic legal authority, the article advances five linked claims: Faqr Symmetry, Juristic Non-Identity, Non-Transferable and Additive Responsibility, Ethical Self-Deliberation under Revelation, and Shūrā as Distributed Corrigibility. Its foundational thesis is deliberately strong: fiqh is a human juristic determination of divine normativity, not revelation itself. desc: Generative AI lowers the cost of literature exploration, argu- ment recombination, drafting, coding scaffolds, and adversarial questioning. For scholars embedded in universities, these gains are absorbed into pre-existing laboratories, seminars, editorial networks, ethics systems, and disciplinary communities. For a standalone scholar, however, AI can create a structurally dif- ferent condition: the production of plausible scholarly objects can become abundant before independent criticism, human relationships, certification, and institutional access become abundant. This article conceptualizes that condition as a prob- lem of scholarly infrastructure reconstruction. It develops a dual-track architecture in which AI-assisted formation, open preprint staging, provenance controls, and machine-constrained checks generate defensible provisional assets, while indepen- dent human friction, repeat correspondence, journal review, and local epistemic participation convert those assets into socially stress-tested knowledge. desc: This article develops a sociology-of-knowledge account of how human religious interpretation can become unusu- ally resistant to correction and, under specific political conditions, contribute to conflict persistence. It begins from a distinction that is doctrinally elementary but sociologically consequential: revelation, human interpre- tation, and institutional authority are not equivalent forms of knowledge. Yet these layers may become so- cially compressed as interpretive judgments are certified by institutions, accumulate symbolic and epistemic au- thority, and become increasingly costly to question. I call this process epistemic hardening. The concept does not designate religious authority, orthodoxy, taqlid, doc- trinal certainty, or sacred commitment as such. Its object is narrower: the declining social revisability of human interpretive claims. The article’s primary rela- tional contribution is asymmetric revisability: the direc- tionally unequal practical capacity to question, correct, reinterpret, classify, or demand justification. Advanced hardening can sediment such asymmetry into durable interpretive stratification and can, under some condi- tions, shift legitimate moral delegation toward protected moral displacement. desc: We compute the k lowest eigenvalues of the generalized banded symmetric problem Kx = λ Mx by bisection on the inertia of the pencil shift K − σ M, evaluated by a banded LDL⊤ factorization in O(nb2 ) work per shift. title: The Declaration Bound: A Bit-Accurate Retained-State Separation for Deferred Spectral Queries
desc: We study exact eigenvalue counting for a streamed real symmetric tridiagonal matrix when the spectral query is announced either before or after the record is read. The principal revision over an arithmetic-register formulation is that retained state is measured in bits and machine words throughout. We construct a 𝑞-ary family of irreducible tridiagonal matrices whose entries and admissible shifts occupy 𝑤 = Θ(log(𝑛𝑞)) bits. A query 𝜎𝑖,𝑟 reveals a threshold predicate of one hidden symbol 𝑎𝑖 , while the complete query-response function determines all 𝑛 symbols. The lower bound applies to every exact solver for the larger class of irreducible symmetric tridiagonal inputs because the constructed family is a subclass. We separately state the classical constant-register Sturm upper bound and explain why it must not be identified with constant bit space without a precision model.

title: The Architecture of Faqr
desc: This article presents a unified constructive framework, within the broad heritage of ahl al-sunna wa-l-jamāʿa, organized by a single insight: creaturely dependence (faqr) is not a defect to be minimized but the positive ontological mode of created being— reality does not entail independence, and the creature is most fully itself where it is most perfectly held. title: Objective Chance and the Priority of Modal Difference
desc: This paper argues that objective chance is not explanatorily primitive. The target is chance-fundamentalism: the view that chance can serve as the primitive explanatory floor of the modal structure in which alternatives and weights are defined. Against this view, I argue that every contentful objective-chance attribution assigns a normalized or measure-like weight to an outcome within a field of alternatives. A field of alternatives requires non-identity among its members, but non-identity alone is insufficient for weightability: the relevant alternatives must remain structurally available for comparison, exclusion, and normalized or measure-like weighting. I call this field-relative condition modal difference. The argument establishes the conceptual and explanatory priority of modal difference over objective chance, while remaining neutral on whether this priority amounts to full metaphysical grounding in the technical sense. The conclusion does not deny chance, indeterminism, quantum probability, or stochastic modelling. It denies only that chance can be explanatorily prior to the modal field required for its own attribution.

title: The Explanatory Insufficiency of Randomness
desc: It is sometimes proposed that objective chance is the terminal explanans of natural order: that laws and their stability are, at bottom, products of brute randomness with nothing more fundamental beneath them. I argue that this position is incoherent as stated. Every contentful ascription of objective chance—whether construed as a property of a process or of a product—presupposes a determinate space of possibilities together with a measure over it. Chance can therefore explain, at most, which possibility is actualised; it cannot explain that the space of possibilities and its measure obtain. The familiar escape routes (statistical “law without law,” self-organisation, the multiverse, quantum indeterminacy, and brute fact) each reinstate or merely relocate this modal structure. I then confront the strongest objection, drawn from Humean supervenience and the Best System Account, together with the suspicion that the argument covertly relies on the Principle of Sufficient Reason. The argument requires only a restricted modal-presupposition principle, not that principle; and the Humean’s own criterion of fit silently presupposes the very structure at issue. The result is interpretation-neutral: it holds wherever a chance is a weight among alternatives, binding frequentist, Humean, and single-case propensity accounts alike. title: Systemic Repair Capacity Theory: A Blood–Lymph–Neural Architecture of Human Health and Chronic Dysregulation
desc: Modern biomedicine has produced a deep, organ-specific knowledge of disease, yet a substantial fraction of clinical suffering — chronic fatigue, persistent pain, post-infectious dysregulation, sleep disruption, brain fog, autonomic instability, and the affective syndromes that accompany them — continues to exceed the explanatory reach of isolated organ models, isolated biomarker panels, and isolated psychiatric categories. title: Marginal Hegemony in Thailand: Satire, the Muslim Minority, and the Politics of Power-Literate Critique
desc: Thai Muslims occupy a layered social position: a religious minority of roughly five percent in a Buddhist-majority constitutional order, yet a community within which some actors exercise coercive moral authority over more vulnerable insiders. This article proposes the concept of marginal hegemony to name the layered condition in which external structural vulnerability and internal domination coexist within a single community field. Drawing on minority-rights theory, the Is Critique Secular? debate, and recent scholarship on queer Southeast Asia, the article locates marginal hegemony at an analytical site that intersectionality, internalized oppression, and minorities-within-minorities frameworks identify but do not specify. An anonymized public-event analysis of a recent urban incident in Bangkok—in which online religious offense escalated through livestream amplification, crowd pressure, and demands for visible public remorse—illustrates three mechanisms: the conversion of moral critique into coercive discipline, the defensive consolidation by which external mockery hardens internal authority, and the double compression of vulnerable insiders. The article closes by proposing a diagnostic framework for what it calls power-literate satire: a mode of public critique that targets specific conduct by identifiable actors with power without converting a marginalized identity into collective stigma. The framework is offered as an analytical tool, not a normative verdict.

desc: This paper introduces the move of catus.kot. i-on-catus.kot. i—the application of N¯ag¯arjuna’s own fourfold negation to the logical procedure itself. The argument shows that no horn of the tetralemma can coherently account for how the catus.kot. i functions as a logical tool, yet the tool continues to function in a reproducible and nonarbitrary way. What survives this self-fold is not nothing: it is a functional residue characterised by four properties—no svabh¯ava, non-emptiness, asymmetric constraint, and specifiable limits. This residue is identified with what the Canon framework calls θ(E): causal-structural organisation that constrains representation without being present as a full, directly accessible ground. Three structural difficulties in Madhyamaka are identified that this analysis surfaces: (i) the non-empty logical relations required for prasa ˙nga to function; (ii) the self-location problem of the two-truths doctrine; and (iii) the circularity of Madhyamaka’s own falsification bar. The paper closes by drawing a principled distinction between philosophy and religion on the basis of independently satisfiable falsification conditions, and locates Madhyamaka and the Canon framework as complementary rather than competing, operating at different but jointly necessary levels of inquiry.

title: Sovereignty, Selection, and Self: A Constructive Ashʿarī Theology of Dependent Order, Directed Selection, and Dependent Identity
desc: This paper proposes three coordinated repairs to classical Ashʿarī theology, each aimed at a structural weakness that the tradition has carried forward without resolving. The first, Dependent Order, offers a three-tiered account of causality that preserves the absolute sovereignty of God at the metaphysical level while making the intelligibility of a sustained world epistemically respectable. In developing it, the paper stakes a positive ontological claim against the charge of illusionism: the causal order of the world is real as the divinely upheld structure of dependable succession (ithbāt al-intiẓām fī al-khalq bi-iqāmat Allāh lahu), and reality does not entail independence. The same tier supports an epistemic bridge from experience to truth: the world resists misunderstanding because God has made it resistant, and knowledge is the residue of beliefs that have survived this resistance. title: Mind as Information Horizon: From Primordial Difference to Expertise Formation on the Discrete Causal Graph
desc: What must reality minimally be if knowingand therefore expertiseare to be possible at all? This paper derives a complete architectonic chain from primordial dierence through the formation of world-class expertise, within a discrete causalinformational ontology. The argument proceeds in ve movements. First, from three postulates (distinguishability, causal closure, nite propagation speed), the telegraph equation on a nite discrete graph is shown to be the unique minimal dynamics governing all structural persistence and decay. Second, the Causal Body Framework and its No-Go theorems are used to derive the Agency-Horizon Theorem (Th-BH): every agent satisfying the framework's axioms exhibits the ve structural properties of an information horizonevent horizon, privacy, emission constraint, partial self-access, and information persistence. This result is a formal theorem, not a metaphor. Third, experience and knowerhood are shown to arise exclusively from the dynamic coupling between the information-horizon agent (mind-core) and embodied brain-body process; neither component alone suces. Fourth, epistemic genesis is derived from the structural impossibility of zero total observation error (εtot > 0 for every nite knower), yielding a formal chain from selection through error-correction to legitimate knowledge. Fifth, expertise is characterized as the mature regime of this coupled system: high persistence, ecient correction, and expanding generative capacity under world-resistance.

title: Relational Alethic Realism: A Causal Metaphysics
desc: This book advances Relational Alethic Realism as a metaphysics-first re- construction of truth, knowledge, intelligence, language, context, selfhood, agency, ethics, and wisdom under conditions of mediation. It begins from the irreducible actuality that awareness is already underway, not to abso- lutize consciousness, but to identify the nearest non-self-canceling starting point for finite reflection. From this floor it argues toward a minimal realist architecture in which world-priority, mediation, non-identity, and irreducible error jointly define the finite condition of inquiry. On that basis, knowledge is reconstructed as corrigible alignment under constraint rather than posses- sion; intelligence as disciplined world-responsive reconfiguration rather than throughput alone; language as an epistemic transport structure rather than a neutral vehicle; context as a field of domain-sensitive evaluation rather than a producer of truth; and wisdom as the practical integration of finite answerability. In an AI-mediated world, the book argues, the future of episte- mology depends on whether human inquiry preserves fallibility, corrigibility, world-answerability, and public criticizability under intensified mediation.

title: When AI Expands Human Potential: Reflective Dissonance, Epistemic Agency, and Constraint
desc: This paper asks a precise question that becomes unavoidable once artificial intelligence is integrated into ordinary thinking, writing, learning, and judgment: when, if ever, does AI expand human potential rather than merely accelerate output? I argue that the answer cannot be given in terms of productivity, convenience, or self-expression alone. AI should instead be understood as a new mediating layer within finite inquiry. Its philosophical significance lies in its capacity either to deepen or to degrade epistemic agency by altering how agents encounter friction, alternative formulations, latent assumptions, and revision pressure. The original intuition that cognitive dissonance with AI can be developmentally fruitful is retained, but it is reconstructed within a stronger framework: constraint-first epistemology. On the view defended here, AI expands human potential only when machine-mediated dissonance becomes disciplined revision under world-answerable conditions. This requires corrigibility, route-openness, criticizability, and domain-sensitive validation. AI can accelerate candidate generation, comparison, and conceptual reframing, but it cannot by itself certify truth, remove irreducible mediation, or replace target- domain assessment. The paper thus offers a middle path between naive AI optimism, pessimistic deskilling narratives, and merely psychological reflectionism. title: Relational Alethic Realism: Truth, Mediation, and Finite World-Tracking after Transparency
desc: This article develops Relational Alethic Realism as a purely metaphysical account of truth under conditions of finite access. Its central claim is that truth is neither transparent identity between thought and world nor the mere outcome of coherence, usefulness, warranted assertibility, or public authorization. Rather, truth is a relation of disciplined answerability between finite representation and a mindindependent order that exceeds present representation while nevertheless constraining it. The paper proceeds in six movements. First, it reconstructs the collapse of the transparency model and argues that finite knowers are world-internal beings whose access is irreducibly mediated. Second, it defends a minimal ontological floor: if truth is to remain world-answerable, reality must possess enough distinction, persistence, causal efficacy, and resistance to constrain representation from beyond representation itself. Third, it argues that finite representation is permanently nonidentical with world-side organization, and that this non-identity yields irreducible error as a structural condition rather than an accidental defect. Fourth, it separates truth-aptness, truth-status, and legitimacy in order to block the recurrent reduction of truth to social authorization or present warrant. title: Constraint-First Epistemology: Normativity, Conditioned Agency, and the Non-Zero Kantian Floor
desc: Both Kantian philosophy and Buddhist thought reject the possibility of epistemic immediacy. Yet contemporary comparative philosophy still lacks a stable account of how normativity survives once cognition is fully acknowledged to be conditioned. If all cognition is mediated, and if agency does not originate from an unconditioned subject, why are some frameworks better than others? This article develops a constraint-first epistemology to address this problem. I argue that finite cognition entails a non-zero floor of mediation—not as a metaphysical essence, but as a structural condition of corrigible inquiry derivable from three minimal premises concerning distinguishability, causal connectivity, and finite propagation speed. From this, normativity is derived as constitutive rather than optional: without responsiveness to constraint, inquiry collapses. The derivation meets the Madhyamaka anti-reification challenge directly by grounding normativity in relational invariants rather than intrinsic natures. Buddhist dependent origination complements this picture by grounding agency in conditioned yet revisable processes rather than in a substantial self. Engaging directly with Evan Thompson, Jay Garfield, and Mark Siderits, I argue that each captures a crucial dimension of the problem— transformability, anti-reification, and reduction of self, respectively—but none fully accounts for the relation between irreducible mediation and structural normativity. title: The Architecture of Mediated Agency: Beyond the Misframing of Free Will and Truth
desc: This article challenges the foundational assumptions of the centuries-old debate on free will and truth by introducing a unified framework of Epistemic Mediation. We argue that the traditional binary between determinism and libertarianism is a structural misframing (Misframing) that ignores the irreducible role of the observer’s eigenstructure. By redefining agency as Deep Authorship—a generative causal organization that functions through a self-model with inherent errors (εtot > 0)— we move beyond the requirement for acausal miracles. Furthermore, we propose that truth is not a ’naked correspondence’ but a Causal-Structural Alignment between the observer’s representation and the world’s generative organization. This framework ’swallows’ the insights of structural realism, predictive coding, and crosscivilizational epistemology, providing a robust account of responsibility without transparency. We demonstrate that the ’gap’ of translation is not a failure to be corrected, but the very condition of human agency and knowledge.

title: Three Layers, One Moon: Premature Category Stabilization and the Structure of Hilal Disagreement
desc: Disagreements over the sighting of the new crescent moon (hilal) recur annually across Muslim communities worldwide, generating persistent conict even among actors who share sincere religious commitment and access to the same astronomical data. This article argues that the primary source of that conict is not astronomical uncertainty, jurisprudential error, or institutional failure, but a structural mechanism: Premature Category Stabilization (PCS), the early freezing of diverse interpretive approaches into simplied templates before sucient layer-specic distinctions have been made. The article introduces a three-layer architecture distinguishing the astronomical layer (visibility conditions), the jurisprudential layer (methods of determining month commencement), and the institutional layer (authority structures and community practices). It shows that most hilal conicts arise not within any single layer but from layer confusion: the application of the tools, standards, and authority claims of one layer to questions that properly belong to another. The article further argues that jurisprudential plurality in this domain is a structural feature of Islamic epistemic tradition, not a failure to converge, and that the appropriate governance response is a repair-permissive community architecture rather than enforced uniformity. title: From Intercultural Marriage to State Policy: Premature Category Stabilization as a Scale-Invariant Mechanism of Cultural Failure
desc: This article develops a scale-bridging theory of Premature Category Stabilization (PCS). First articulated in the context of Muslim-friendly tourism, PCS names the process by which diverse persons and groups are frozen into simplied institutional templates prior to encounter. The article argues that this is not a sectorbound service failure but a general mechanism of intercultural breakdown recurring across family mediation, community institutions, public services, tourism systems, and state policy. Drawing on the cultural imaginary framework, the paper reconceptualizes culture as a stable eigenmode cluster composed of shared decoders, value-weights, and lifecycle templates. It further denes peace structurally through three necessary conditions: pathway openness, feasibility preservation, and repairpermissiveness. The central claim is that cultural harm emerges when symbolic recognition or accommodation outruns operational calibration and institutions begin acting on their own compressed model of a group rather than on the living plurality before them. The article concludes by specifying the framework's limits, proof obligations, and implications for intercultural governance, policy design, and comparative research. Keywords: cultural imaginary; premature category stabilization; multiculturalism; structural violence; intercultural governance; peace theory; public policy; family mediation; tourism studies; repair-permissiveness

title: Beyond Halal Labels: Premature Category Stabilization in Muslim-Friendly Tourism
desc: Muslim-friendly tourism has expanded from a niche market concern into a visible strategic domain in global tourism and hospitality. Existing scholarship has established that halal-friendly attributes, Islamic destination features, and Muslim-compatible service provisions can influence destination choice, perceived value, and tourist satisfaction. At the same time, these visible assurances do not consistently translate into stronger trust, conversion, revisit intention, or durable market performance across tourism settings. Although prior research also recognizes that Muslim travelers are heterogeneous in religiosity, cultural background, trip purpose, family form, and service expectations, it has not yet sufficiently theorized how this diversity is interpreted and operationalized by tourism providers and policy systems. This article argues that a central source of underperformance lies in premature category stabilization: the early reduction of diverse Muslim travelers into rigid, provider-defined service categories. It proposes a mechanism in which provider-centered category projection shapes service templates, promise framing, and interactional conduct in ways that generate expectation mismatch, relational miscalibration, and trust erosion across the tourism journey. title: Causal Qualia: A Constraint Theory of Phenomenal Interior
desc: Why internal information processing should ever be accompanied by phenomenal experience remains one of the central questions in philosophy of mind. Yet the hard problem is often posed in a form so broad that it obscures distinctions that matter theoretically. This article develops a constraint-based approach intended to sharpen that terrain. Rather than attempting to derive consciousness outright, it separates several structural questions that are frequently conated with phenomenality itself, including the privacy of experience, partial self-opacity, and rst-person asymmetry, treating each as a consequence of bounded causal organization rather than as a brute metaphysical given. The central claim is that privacy alone cannot explain phenomenality. Hidden information, internal integration, or computational complexity are not sucient. What matters is the organization of interior state within a causal architecture in which an embodied agent models its own condition under bounded access, regulatory dependence, and aective stakes. On this basis, the paper proposes a candidate architecture for phenomenal interior consisting of a bounded interior horizon, self-indexed modeling, embodied homeostatic coupling, valence, ownership binding, cross-layer coherence, grounding in bodyworld interaction, and temporally persistent causal memory. title: The Civilization of Knowledge: Who Has the Authority to Interpret the World
desc: Standard accounts of knowledge history often describe human civilization as a gradual ascent from myth to reason, from religion to science, and from science to artificial intelligence. This article argues that such narratives remain incomplete. What changes across civilizations is not only the accumulation of truths, but the succession of agencies authorized to interpret the world’s signals and stabilize those interpretations as social reality. The article develops a comparative framework organized around five linked terms: signal, translation, stabilization, agency, and conflict. Human beings do not encounter reality as a complete and transparent whole; they encounter partial traces, anomalies, records, measurements, and mediated signs. These do not become knowledge by themselves. They must be translated into meaningful accounts, stabilized through repeatable and durable forms, and socially authorized through institutions, procedures, or recognized interpreters. The history of knowledge can therefore be read as the history of changing interpretive authority. Across the longue duree, this article traces major shifts from embodied and oral interpreters to priestly and archival regimes, from philosophical and translational formations to scientific, professional, and media institutions, and finally to platforms, algorithms, and AI-mediated systems. Its central claim is that knowledge crises are often authority crises: moments in which the legitimacy of interpreters is contested

title: Knowledge as Stabilized Translation: Toward an Observer-Constrained Epistemology
desc: Epistemology has often treated knowledge as a matter of access: a subject seeks justified, reliable, or rational contact with reality. This article argues that such accounts remain incomplete because they understate the constitutive role of mediation, finite access, selective encoding, and structured error. The problem becomes sharper in the age of artificial intelligence, where systems generate reliable and action-guiding outputs without fitting inherited models of reflective belief or transparent justification. I propose that epistemology should begin not from direct access to reality, but from bounded observers who form world-models under constraint. On this view, knowledge is best understood as stabilized translation under bounded observation: a representation that remains stable across admissible variation, calibration, and cross-checking. The result is a framework that preserves realism without naïvety, fallibilism without skepticism, and provides a common grammar for human and machine forms of model-based knowing. Keywords: epistemology; knowledge; observation; mediation; artificial intelligence; translation; realism

title: The Causal Grammar of Structured Coexistence: Conflict, Violence, Repair, and Non-Suppressive Peace
desc: Sociological and philosophical traditions have developed extensive explanations of social structure, conflict, violence, and peace. Yet these phenomena are often analyzed within partially separate theoretical frameworks. As a result, disagreement is frequently conflated with conflict, conflict with violence, and stability with peace. This article proposes a causal grammar linking five concepts: structure, conflict, violence, repair, and peace. Social structures organize fields of feasible possibility within shared social environments. Conflict emerges when actors attempt to sustain structures that cannot be jointly reproduced. Violence occurs when incompatibility compresses actors’ feasible life-space. Repair denotes the protected reopening of damaged relations, while peace refers to stable coexistence that preserves actors’ possibilities and maintains the capacity for repair. The framework provides a compact diagnostic vocabulary for distinguishing difference from conflict, conflict from violence, and stable order from non-suppressive peace. Keywords: conflict; violence; peace; social theory; political sociology

title: Neutrality Beyond Visual Sameness: Judicial Impartiality, Human Fallibility, and Institutional Design
desc: Debates about judicial neutrality frequently assume that visible religious attire threatens impartial adjudication. Yet existing legal debates about religious symbols rarely integrate empirical research on judicial cognition and decision-making. This article argues that the assumption linking visible identity to judicial bias rests on a mistaken premise. Empirical research in behavioral law and legal psychology demonstrates that judges, like all human decision-makers, remain susceptible to systematic cognitive distortions, including anchoring, framing effects, hindsight bias, and implicit bias. Because these distortions arise from the architecture of human cognition rather than from visible identity markers, regulating religious attire cannot plausibly eliminate the sources of adjudicative bias. Legal systems instead attempt to manage human fallibility through institutional safeguards such as adversarial procedure, evidentiary discipline, reason-giving requirements, appellate review, and collegial deliberation. The article further shows that appearance-based neutrality rules risk producing structural exclusion by disproportionately burdening religious minorities while lacking a demonstrated causal connection to improved adjudicative accuracy. title: Gettier, Instability, and the Structural Condition on Knowledge
desc: Since Gettier, epistemologists have repeatedly attempted to repair the justifiedtrue-belief model by adding further conditions designed to exclude accidental truth. Yet the most striking feature of post-Gettier epistemology is not the ingenuity of these repairs but their failure to converge. This paper argues that the persistent non-convergence of post-Gettier analyses is best explained by a mislocation of the explanandum. Proposition-level theories evaluate completed beliefs and therefore underdescribe the structural fragility in the representational route connecting belief to world. The paper proposes a structural reconstruction: knowledge is the stabilization of representation under admissible variation. On this view, epistemic luck is representational instability. I first diagnose the repair cycle of post-Gettier epistemology and argue that proposition-first analysis systematically omits formation-path fragility. I then introduce admissible stability as a condition on objective epistemic success and reconstruct epistemic luck as instability under admissible transformation. Finally, I apply the framework to three canonical cases—fake barn, stopped clock, and Smith–Jones—and argue that these cases are unified as distinct forms of representational instability. If correct, the lesson of Gettier is not that knowledge requires one more clause, but that epistemology has been analyzing the wrong kind of object.

title: Causal Agency  A Persistence Control Theory of Adaptive Systems
desc: Agency is a central concept across philosophy of action, cognitive science, theoretical biol- ogy, and artificial intelligence. Despite extensive research across these fields, existing accounts remain theoretically fragmented because they are typically grounded in domain-specific mech- anisms and operate at different explanatory levels. Philosophical theories emphasize inten- tional action and rational deliberation, biological theories focus on metabolic self-maintenance, and computational models define agents primarily in terms of goal-directed decision processes. While each of these perspectives captures important aspects of agency, none provides a struc- tural account capable of explaining agency across the full spectrum of adaptive systems. This paper proposes a structural theory of agency based on a persistence–control frame- work. Within this framework, systems are interpreted as dynamical systems operating under constraint structures that shape the possible trajectories of their states. Persistence is defined as the continued occupation of a viable region of state space that allows the system to main- tain its organization or functional identity. Agency emerges when the internal dynamics of a system are capable of regulating or modifying the constraint structures that govern its own persistence. title: Symmetry-Invariant Knowledge as Fixed Points of Observer-Translation Dynamics
desc: Three foundational problems in the philosophy of science—Hume’s problem of induction, Goodman’s new riddle of projectibility, and Hempel’s raven paradox—are standardly treated as independent puzzles requiring separate solutions. We resolve all three simultaneously by introducing a dynamical framework in which knowledge acquisition is modelled as an equivariant learning operator on a hypothesis space equipped with a regime-specific group action. Our central result, the CMP Knowledge Stability Theorem, establishes that under an equivariance condition and a Lyapunov ascent condition on a quality functional, every stable attractor of the learning dynamics lies in the set of hypotheses invariant under the admissible transformation group of the operative regime. Goodman’s grue predicate fails because it is not invariant under time-translation in a stationary regime; the white-shoe evidence fails to confirm the raven hypothesis because its causal relevance score is identically zero. title: Health as Constraint-Admissible Trajectory A Genesis–CMP Aligned Minimal Metaphysics of Health
desc: This paper articulates a domain-restricted, constraint- first metaphysics of health aligned with a process- structural ontology (Genesis framework) and trajectory- based admissibility logic (CMP). Health is defined not as equilibrium, statistical normality, or moral fitness, but as the maintained dispositional capacity of a temporally exposed vulnerable integrated process to preserve its identity-pattern through constraint-admissible reconsti- tution across state-transitions. Four conceptual necessities are identified: vulnerabil- ity, temporality, integrative organization, and identity- preserving reconstitutability. Identity is redefined as admissible continuity of identity-defining integration across constraint-governed transitions rather than static structural sameness. A polyphase identity thesis accom- modates regime shifts (e.g., developmental phase transi- tions), and a transformative recovery clause distinguishes identity-content change from loss of identity-defining integration. Health is thereby secured against reduc- tionism, equilibrium fetishism, teleology, and static sub- stance ontology, while remaining minimally grounded

title: Invariance and the Identity of a World A Minimal Structural Necessity Thesis
desc: When distinct descriptions are said to concern the same world, what makes this claim more than pragmatic coordination or mutual translation? Absent structural constraint, world-identity risks collapsing into representationindexing or community agreement. This paper argues that same-world discourse presupposes a non-empty invariant structural core: at least some claims must remain stable under independently motivated admissible transformations. The invariant core need not be metaphysically fundamental or exhaustive; it must be structurally stable. Without such invariance, cross-framework disagreement loses world-directed normativity. The invariance requirement is neither empirical nor analytic but functions as a condition-of-intelligibility necessity governing world-reference

title: Causal Memory Admissibility (CMAP): A Structural Necessity Classication Discrete-First, Primitives-Grounded, Domain-Independent
desc: What constitutive memory structures are compatible with causality and passivity under finite resources? Starting from two pre-theoretic primitives -- retardation (causal order prior to geometry) and finite-resource admissibility -- we prove the Causal Memory Admissibility Theorem (CMAP): a bidirectional necessity-and-uniqueness classification of retarded constitutive memory operators on finite records. Under a finite-resource admissible class (H1-H4) and five structural gates (P1) retardation, (P2) operator passivity, (F1+F2) genuine fading, (N) non-negativity, and (A) diffusive admissibility, admissible memory is uniquely constrained to be Completely Monotone Finite-resource (CMF): a non-negative-weight superposition of geometric-decay channels, with rates strictly in (0,1). Conversely, any CMF kernel certifies all five gates, yielding a bidirectional (<=>) admissibility certificate. All proof steps use only finite sequences and finite operators; continuum notation appears solely as optional encoding. Two class-conditional no-go results follow: (NG1) Markovian constitutive laws fail the genuine-fading gate and are structurally excluded. (NG2) the admissible class is open -- both the zero-rate limit (infinite persistence) and the unit-rate limit (Markovian) lie outside the class. title: Learning Under Generative Abundance: A Structural Law of Epistemic Stabilization
desc: Artificial intelligence creates an epistemic environment in which coherent expressions can be produced externally at near-zero marginal cost. This paper argues that the consequences for education stem not primarily from pedagogical choice, but from a structural law governing inference under conditions of generative abundance. A single underlying dynamic gives rise to three observable effects: degradation of inferential signals, escalation of conceptual volatility, and the emergence of selective stabilization. Beyond a critical threshold of generative exposure, learning undergoes a regime shift — from accumulation to discrimination. Learning is therefore redefined as the capacity to preserve structural stability when expressive production no longer uniquely indicates internal organization. title: Faith in Service Systems: Dynamics of Cultural-Based Practitioners in Creating Shared Spaces among State, Market, and Religion
desc: This article examines the role of Cultural-Based Practitioners (CBP) who operate at the intersection of state, market, and religion amid the rapid transformations of the ASEAN digital economy. It argues that faith is not an impediment to development but a profound ethical and human-centric foundation for creating service systems that honor religious identity without commodifying it. The paper introduces the CBP framework , integrating cultural skills, cultural bridging, and cultural governance to form a Living Soft Infrastructure —a model for transforming faith-based and cultural capital into verifiable social and economic value. Case studies from Thailand, Singapore, and Taiwan demonstrate how individual, institutional, and state-level practitioners can sustain coexistence through transparency, justice, and shared ethical values.

title: AI, Translation, and Access to Event-Specific Contex
desc: This article is published under an Open Civil Science framework by the author as an independent scholarly work. It has not undergone formal journal peer review at the time of release. All claims are explicitly framed as conceptual and non-empirical. This paper presents a conceptual framework for analyzing how artificial intelligence reshapes human access to meaning through changes in contextual mediation. Situating AI within a historical and socio-technical evolution of interpretation, the paper distinguishes between eventspecific context associated with real-world events and interpretive context available to human agents. It argues that while AI systems substantially expand access to interpreted information and linguistic synthesis, they do not reconstruct the full situational, temporal, relational, and agency-bearing conditions of events. The contribution is fourfold: (i) a structural distinction between information access and context access; (ii) a historical–structural model of context transformation across offline, searchbased, social-media, and AI-mediated epochs; (iii) explicit theoretical constructs including the external context-frame (), interaction efficiency (), and a principled separation between grounding and embodiment; and (iv) a hypothesis and boundary set specifying conditions under which AI interaction tends to support or degrade human agency. The paper advances an Open Civil Science orientation and makes no empirical claims. Keywords: AI; translation and

title: Social Enterprise Survival Under Realistic Margins via Lead Multiplier, Growth Cost, and Action Lag
desc: Abstract. We present Translated Trust Dynamics v3 (TTD v3), a minimal dynamical-systems framework for social enterprise (SE) survival under capitalist market conditions with realistic margins (∼10%). TTD v3 extends v2 with three practitioner-grounded mechanisms: (1) a symbolic-trust lead multiplier β whereby reputation opens market access but does not directly generate revenue, (2) a growth cost γ that scales overhead with cash accumulation, preventing unrealistic wealth buildup, and (3) action lag ℓ whereby trust and hazard effects manifest after 1–2 periods rather than immediately.
